goal: Ben (drawn young, about five years old) points up at a big yellow toy pan on the top shelf of the toy kitchen. The tip of a fluffy golden-brown tail hangs over the edge of the pan. No letters, words, or numbers anywhere.
colorPrompt: Compose one children's book picture from the element pictures. Picture 1 shows the boy Ben (the approved 3D character; ignore the gray background and the shadow). Picture 2 is the empty play corner of the same kindergarten classroom: a low wooden shelf with two shelves at the left (it holds a few cups and plates; the toy pans of this page stand on it too), and a child-height wooden toy kitchen at the right with a toy stove, a sink, two cupboard doors, and a high top shelf; use it as the background and keep the same room. Picture 3 shows the puppy Pip in four 3D views (the flat drawing at the top is only a hint). Picture 4 shows the three toy pans: the SMALL RED pan (middle size), the TINY BLUE pan (the smallest; it fits inside the red pan), and the BIG YELLOW pan (the largest, about twice as wide as the red pan); each is a shallow round pan with one short straight handle. Keep the soft, round, bright 3D render look of the pictures, not a 2D drawing and no outlines. The children keep their chibi proportions: a big head and a small body. Hands are small, chubby child hands with five clear short fingers (four fingers and one thumb) when open, never fists unless stated, and a hanging hand shows relaxed, separate short fingers. Rendering errors to NOT copy from the character pictures: a tiny dark tick mark or pale skin flap at the outer corner of an eye, and a faint pale crease on a forehead. Each eye ends in a smooth, rounded corner; Nan alone keeps one short, thick, curved eyelash flick at each outer eye corner. Clean eye corners, no streak on the forehead, no marks on the face. The ears are smooth, with one clean rounded rim. Each piece of clothing is one even color with no pale patches, no pale blotches at the shoulders, and no stains. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no writing on any picture or sign. The picture is for young children and is rated G. Keep each character exactly as in the pictures: Ben: short messy light-brown hair, big brown eyes, a light-blue T-shirt, dark-blue shorts, grey sneakers. The picture: Ben points up at the big yellow toy pan on the top shelf. A medium shot at a low camera height in the play corner (picture 2), the toy kitchen large at the right. The BIG YELLOW pan (picture 4) stands on the HIGH top shelf of the toy kitchen with its handle toward the front. The tip of a fluffy golden-brown tail (picture 3) hangs over the edge of the pan, a small part only. Ben stands at the bottom left on the floor, tilts his head back, and points up at the pan with the index finger of one hand; his other hand hangs relaxed. He looks up with wide eyes and a hopeful small smile. Only the named children are in the picture as people. The puppy Pip is NOT in the picture: only the tip of his fluffy golden-brown tail shows over the edge of the pan, and no other part of him. Picture 3 shows the puppy Pip: copy only the golden-brown color and the fluffy shape of his tail; the puppy himself must not appear.The page text is "Can I get the pan?" and is context only: do not draw any text.
linePrompt: Picture 1 is a 3D-rendered children's book picture. Convert picture 1 to line art for a student book: thick, even black lines (about three times a normal outline), simple closed shapes that a 5-year-old can color, on pure white. No blush circles, no eyelash ticks, no hair strands, no shading, no gray, no texture lines, no text. Keep every shape in the same place and the same size. Draw each eye as a closed outline with a big solid black pupil (a filled black circle) inside it. Draw the mouth exactly as in picture 1: an open mouth stays an open mouth drawn as a closed outline, and a closed smile stays one curve. Draw each hand as a closed outline with each finger as a separate rounded shape. Each head of hair is one closed shape. The ear is one closed outline with at most one inner curve. No lines on the clothes other than the outline, the collar, and the star. Simplify the background: draw only a few large, simple, closed shapes (the floor line, the wall line, two or three big closed beam shapes, the window as one closed square, each easel as one closed frame, the table as one closed shape, the toy kitchen and the shelf as large closed box shapes). No wood grain lines, no floor plank lines, no plaster texture, no hatching, no tick marks, no small details on the shelf. Every outline is one closed line that never runs into a background line; no loose line ends anywhere. Every line inside an object ends on another line. Use few background shapes. Each toy pan is one closed round shape with its inner rim as one closed oval, and its handle is one closed shape. The pans have no pattern. The tail tip is one closed rounded shape.
